title: filo-go vs binwalk — measured wall-clock timings
method: Median of 3 wall-clock runs per (tool, file), captured with Python time.perf_counter(). Full process invocation included; no warm-cache tricks.
notes: The speedup is real, not just startup overhead — even on the 10MB file scan-time dominates and filo-go is still 13.94x faster.
The gap narrows as file size grows (216x -> 194x -> 14x); binwalk's per-byte cost catches up but filo-go's single-pass architecture keeps a large constant-factor advantage.
filo-go flagged the synthetic PNG as missing its IEND chunk; binwalk --quiet did not (binwalk does not validate PNG structure, only scans for embedded signatures).
Single-competitor scope by design; extending to exiftool/yara/file/sha256sum is a one-line change in competitor_bench.sh.
Earlier synthesized numbers in filo-go-web's site-content.ts (e.g. 'Hash Comp. 6.2x', 'Strings 15,078x') have been replaced with these measured numbers in a companion patch.
schema_match: Object shape matches the BENCHMARKS const in apps/web/src/data/site-content.ts ({name, filo, binwalk, unit, speedup}). The web app does not currently read this JSON file directly — it imports the hardcoded TS array. A follow-up could add a build step that reads this JSON and generates the TS array, so the web app and the bench script share a single source of truth.
